'''Asher A. Friesem''' ({{Langx|he|אשר פריזם}}) is a professor at the [[Weizmann Institute of Science]] in [[Israel]].{{Citation needed|date=May 2010}}

Friesem received B.Sc. and Ph.D. degrees from the [[University of Michigan]] in 1958 and 1968, respectively. From 1958 to 1963 he was employed by [[Bell Aero Systems]] Company and [[Bendix Research Laboratories]]. From 1963 to 1969, at the [[University of Michigan Institute for Social Research|University of Michigan’s Institutes]] of Science and Technology, he conducted investigations in [[coherent optics]], mainly in the areas of [[optical data processing]] and [[holography]]. From 1969 to 1973, he was principal research engineer in the Electro-Optics Center of [[Harris Corporation|Harris, Inc.]], performing research in the areas of optical memories and displays.{{Citation needed|date=May 2010}}<ref>{{cite news |last1=Rosen |first1=Marcella |title=65 years of innovation, from Rummikub to the 'God Particle' |url=https://www.timesofisrael.com/65-years-of-innovation-from-rummikub-to-the-god-particle/ |accessdate=3 July 2019 |publisher=Times of Israel |date=15 April 2013}}</ref>

In 1973 he joined the staff of the Weizmann Institute of Science, Israel and was appointed professor of optical sciences in 1977. He subsequently served as department head, chairman of the scientific council, and chairman of the professorial council. In recent years his research activities have concentrated on new holographic concepts and applications, optical image processing, electro-optic devices, and new [[laser resonator]] configurations.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.optoiq.com/index/photonics-technologies-applications/lfw-display/lfw-article-display/250399/articles/laser-focus-world/volume-42/issue-3/world-news/laser-optics-sixteen-laser-beams-combined-with-88-efficiency.html|title=Laser optics: : Sixteen laser beams combined with 88% efficiency|last=Overton|first=Gail|date=1 March 2006|publisher=OptoIQ|accessdate=21 September 2010| archiveurl= https://web.archive.org/web/20100924004208/http://www.optoiq.com/index/photonics-technologies-applications/lfw-display/lfw-article-display/250399/articles/laser-focus-world/volume-42/issue-3/world-news/laser-optics-sixteen-laser-beams-combined-with-88-efficiency.html| archivedate= 24 September 2010 | url-status= live}}</ref>

He has served on numerous program and advisory committees of national and international conferences. Among other posts, he served for many years as a vice president of the International Commission of Optics ([[International Commission for Optics|ICO]]) and chairman of the Israel [[Laser and Electro-Optics Society]]. He is a [[fellow]] of [[Optical Society|OSA]], a life fellow of [[IEEE]], and member of [[SPIE]] and [[Sigma Xi]]. In 2018, he received the [[Emmett N. Leith Medal]], "For pioneering, seminal and wide ranging contributions to coherent optics, particularly the developments of new techniques and procedures in holographic applications and optical information processing."<ref>{{Cite web |title=Emmett N. Leith Medal {{!}} Optica |url=https://www.optica.org/get_involved/awards_and_honors/awards/award_descriptions/leith/ |access-date=2024-09-06 |website=www.optica.org}}</ref> Over the years he has been a visiting professor in [[Germany]], [[Switzerland]], [[France]] and the [[United States|U.S.]], has authored and co-authored more than 250 scientific papers, co-editor of four scientific volumes, and holds over 30 international patents.{{Citation needed|date=May 2010}}

He made the first full-color [[hologram]].{{Citation needed|date=February 2010}}
